title: Signs a Root Canal May Be Failing
metaTitle: Signs a Root Canal May Be Failing: What to Watch
metaDescription: Returning pain, swelling or a gum bump can signal a failing root canal. Learn the warning signs and when retreatment may save the tooth, in Markham.
excerpt: Returning pain, swelling, or a gum bump can signal a failing root canal. Learn the warning signs and why retreatment may still save the tooth.
heroImageAlt: Diagram of a tooth with a small bump on the adjacent gum indicating a possible failing root canal.
bodyHtml:
A root canal that is starting to fail often announces itself with returning pain, tenderness when you bite, swelling, or a small pimple-like bump on the gum near the tooth. Sometimes there are no symptoms at all, and a problem is only spotted on a routine X-ray. If a previously treated tooth starts bothering you again, it does not automatically mean the tooth is lost — but it is a reason to have it checked, because options such as retreatment may be available.

Why a treated tooth can run into trouble later

Root canal treatment has a high success rate, but no dental treatment works every time. A tooth can develop problems months or years later for several reasons: a canal that was especially narrow or curved, a new crack, a leaking or lost restoration that let bacteria back in, or decay creeping in at the edges. The good news is that many of these situations can be reassessed, and a tooth that seems to be failing can sometimes be saved again.

Common signs a root canal may be failing

  • Pain that returns — a dull ache, throbbing, or sharp twinges in a tooth that had settled down after treatment.
  • Tenderness when biting or pressing — discomfort when you chew on that tooth, or when it is tapped.
  • Swelling — of the gum, cheek, or face near the tooth, which may come and go.
  • A gum bump or “pimple” — a small spot on the gum (a sinus tract) that may drain and then reappear. It can relieve pressure, so it is not always painful, but it signals ongoing infection.
  • Tooth discolouration — darkening of a previously treated tooth.
  • Bad taste or odour — sometimes linked to drainage from infection.

Any one of these is worth a dental assessment. Several together make it more likely that something needs attention. It also helps to notice whether a symptom is new, or whether it has been coming and going for a while, as a recurring pattern can be an important clue for your dentist.

Sometimes there are no symptoms

Not every failing root canal hurts. Chronic, low-grade infection can be painless, and the first sign may be a shadow on a radiograph seen during a check-up. This is one reason regular dental visits and X-rays matter even after a tooth has been treated — they can catch a quiet problem before it becomes a painful one.

What happens if a root canal is failing?

Your dentist will examine the tooth and usually take an X-ray to see what is happening around the root. Depending on the findings, options can include root canal retreatment (reopening, re-cleaning, and re-sealing the canals), in some cases a surgical approach, or — if the tooth cannot be saved — extraction with a plan to replace it. The aim is usually to keep your natural tooth when that is realistic. You can read more about root canal retreatment at Smile Dental Arts Centre to understand what that process involves.

Is a failing root canal an emergency?

Not always, but it should not be ignored. Significant swelling, fever, or spreading pain deserves prompt care. Milder, nagging symptoms still warrant an appointment so the tooth can be assessed before things progress.

Can a failed root canal be fixed without pulling the tooth?

Often, yes. Retreatment or minor surgery can resolve many cases. Whether that is the best route for your tooth depends on the specifics, which a dentist will discuss with you.

Does a gum pimple always mean the root canal failed?

A recurring bump on the gum near a treated tooth commonly points to infection that needs attention, but only an examination and X-ray can confirm the cause.

When to get it checked

If a tooth that had a root canal starts to ache, feels tender, swells, or grows a stubborn gum bump, book an assessment rather than waiting to see if it passes. Dr. Neda Kadivar, a general and family dentist with over 20 years of experience, can evaluate a previously treated tooth at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham, Ontario, and talk through the options for keeping it where possible.

This article is general information and not a substitute for professional dental advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always speak with a licensed dentist about your specific situation.
